acceptance: A core PR that changes the CLI option or platform registry used by a site docs example gets an advisory check reporting whether the site builds from its bundle
A deliberately broken docs example in a test PR makes the check fail; the check is not in the required contexts
Core still contains no JS/TS or package.json
context: Found 2026-10-17 at site-split closeout. Must not become a required context; D17 allows no further ruleset change. Rescoped after core PR 3658 covered path deletions.
description:
Rescoped 2026-10-28. Decision D5 of the site-repo split ADR (docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md) means a core change that breaks the site build is found only after merge: the site refuses the bundle, keeps the last good site and opens an issue. Since the site authors the docs, a docs/-only trigger is stale. Core PR check_site_linked_paths (make site-linked-paths-check, in ci-paths) now catches the observed failure, deletion or rename of a core path that a site docs page links to. The residual gap is any other core change that makes the site converter, docs:check (block mode) or a deploy gate fail on the new bundle, for example a renamed CLI option or platform that a docs example uses, or a bundle member change. The ADR names an advisory pre-merge build as a follow-up. No core workflow builds the site before merge; the only reference to benchbox-site in core workflows is the post-merge dispatch in .github/workflows/site-inputs.yml.

Add a non-required check on core PRs that touch bundle-producing paths (site-inputs inputs: benchbox/ CLI and platform registries, doc contracts, results data, scripts/site_inputs.py): build the PR's site-inputs bundle and ask the site repo to build it (for example a dispatch that reports back as a check), without adding Node to core (ADR D9). Needs a cross-repo token the owner must provision; do not start before that decision.
